heading: INT. SUNSET SOUND STUDIO - CONTROL ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SUNSET SOUND STUDIO - CONTROL ROOM - NIGHT
Egg-crate foam, a mixing desk the size of a pool table.
Beyond the glass, a vocal booth with a single microphone.
DAVID KESSLER, 50s, producer, sits at the desk.
Next to him is DAVID KESSEL, 20s, an intern who has been mistaken for him all week.
KIM, singer, 30s, stands in the booth.
Her brother KIP, 30s, leans on the wall of the control room eating a sandwich nobody offered him.
Over the talkback, the engineer, RHONDA, 40s, speaks from somewhere in the building.
Is everyone rolling or is it just me
units.name: RHONDA

units.text: Kim, honey, we are on take forty-one. I'm going to say this one time with love. The song is about heartbreak. You sound like you're ordering a coffee.
units.name: DAVID KESSLER

units.text: Maybe I am ordering a coffee. Maybe that's the heartbreak. Maybe heartbreak is mostly just standing in a line.
units.name: KIM

units.text: That's actually good. You should say that on the record.
units.name: KIP

units.text: Sorry, hi, I think that's David's note to give. Mine. Not mine. His.
units.name: DAVID KESSEL

units.text: Kessel, you can't be both.
units.name: DAVID KESSLER

units.text: I'm just saying I wrote the bridge.
units.name: DAVID KESSEL

units.text: He wrote the bridge, Kip wrote the chorus, and I wrote the part where I leave.
units.name: KIM

units.text: Great news the part where you leave is cheaper to mix
units.name: RHONDA

units.text: Kim. Are you leaving us or the song?
units.name: KIP

units.text: I don't know. Roll the tape.
units.name: KIM

units.text: Press record.
units.name: DAVID KESSLER

units.text: Rolling. Take forty-two.
units.name: DAVID KESSEL
